correctness.rationale: For every two-part base, rectangle parity forces rank-one binary cross orientations. The type-counting bijection splits extensions into a new class (2^n binary choices) and two existing classes (two complementary row/column choices each), giving the exact polynomial. The four residual exponent occurrences must be grouped by one of three perfect matchings; every admissible grouping is constructible. Each matching leaves at most one orientation bit modulo independent row/column relabellings, hence at most two isomorphism types. Three genuinely distinct profiles need four distinct nonnegative exponents, forcing n>=6; exponents 0,1,2,3 realize all three profiles with two types each. The direct independent extension/quotient enumerator checked all 342 binary matrices through seven vertices and returned VERIFY_OK. No finite test is used to prove the all-size bound.
